title: Finite integral coefficients admit a condensed two-term finite free resolution
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ with its valuation topology [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with the discrete topology and let $a:O\to A$ be a continuous unital ring homomorphism. Regard $A$ as an $O$-module through $a$. Write $\underline O(S)=C(S,O)$ and $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for the condensed ring sheaves on the site of profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], and use module objects over $\underline O$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. There exist an integer $r\geq0$, an $O$-linear surjection $q:O^r\to A$ and an $O$-linear map $\phi:O^r\to O^r$ given by a matrix with entries in $O$ such that $q$ is continuous, $\phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\ker q$ with its subspace topology, and
$$0\longrightarrow O^r\xrightarrow{\phi}O^r\xrightarrow q A\longrightarrow0$$
is exact as a sequence of $O$-modules. For every profinite set $S$, applying continuous functions gives an exact sequence of abelian groups
$$0\longrightarrow C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{\phi\circ-}C(S,O^r)\xrightarrow{q\circ-}C(S,A)\longrightarrow0.$$
In particular $0\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline O^{\oplus r}\to\underline A\to0$ is an exact sequence of condensed $\underline O$-modules. The assertion includes $A=0$, for which $r=0$ is allowed.
